back: Nucleophile donates an electron pair; electrophile accepts one.
Both bonding electrons go to one fragment, forming ions.
H₂ (Ni) → alkane; X₂ → dihalide; HX → halogenoalkane; H₂O (H₃PO₄) → alcohol.
Acid: electron-pair acceptor. Base: electron-pair donor. Together they form a coordination bond.
Primary; one step; rate = k[RX][Nu]; inversion of configuration; aprotic solvent.
Tertiary; carbocation intermediate; rate = k[RX]; racemic product; protic solvent.
Major product comes from the more stable carbocation (3° > 2° > 1°).
Conc. HNO₃ + H₂SO₄ → NO₂⁺; electrophilic substitution → nitrobenzene.
